citations.quote: A total of 536 patients were randomized (1:1) to margetuximab plus chemotherapy (n=266) or

trastuzumab plus chemotherapy (n=270). Randomization was stratified by chemotherapy choice (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine), number of lines of therapy in the metastatic setting (\le 2, > 2), and number of metastatic sites (\le 2, > 2).

result.text: Median PFS 5.8 months (95% CI 5.5, 7.0) vs 4.9 months (95% CI 4.2, 5.6); stratified HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.59, 0.98); p=0.033. OS immature: median 21.6 vs 19.8 months (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.69, 1.13; p=0.2086). ORR 22% vs 16%.

citations.quote: The median PFS in the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm was 5.8 months (95% CI: 5.5, 7.0) compared to a median PFS of 4.9 months (95%CI: 4.2, 5.6) in the trastuzumab plus chemotherapy arm corresponding to a stratified hazard ratio of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.59, 0.98).

Median PFS in the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm was 5.8 months (95% CI: 5.5, 7.0) compared to 4.9 months (95% CI: 4.2, 5.6) in the trastuzumab plus chemotherapy arm (HR = 0.76; 95% CI: 0.59, 0.98; p = 0.033).

The median OS was 21.6 months (95% CI: 17.7, 23.8) in the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm compared to 19.8 months (95% CI: 15.5, 21.2) in the trastuzumab plus chemotherapy arm (HR 0.89; 95% CI: 0.69, 1.13; p=0.2086).
The objective response rate (ORR) was 22% (95% CI: 17%, 27%) in the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm vs 16% (95% CI: 12%, 20%) in the trastuzumab arm.

target_moa.text: Margetuximab-cmkb, a HER2/neu receptor antagonist, is a chimeric Fc-engineered IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds the extracellular domain of HER2, inhibits tumor cell proliferation, reduces shedding of the HER2 extracellular domain, and mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).

citations.quote: Margetuximab-cmkb, a HER2/neu receptor antagonist, is a chimeric Fc-engineered IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody. Margetuximab-cmkb binds to the extracellular domain of the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 protein (HER2). Margetuximab mediates antibody-dependent cytotoxicity (ADCC) in HER2-positive cancer cell lines using effector cells from human donors of all CD16A genotypes and promotes NK-cell activation and cytolytic activity.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were fatigue/asthenia, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, headache, pyrexia, alopecia, abdominal pain, peripheral neuropathy, arthralgia/myalgia, cough, decreased appetite, dyspnea, infusion-related reactions, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, and extremity pain. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 16% of margetuximab-plus-chemotherapy patients. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.1%. Left ventricular dysfunction occurred in 1.9%; infusion-related reactions in 13%.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (>10%) experienced by patients in the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm were fatigue/asthenia, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, headache, pyrexia, alopecia, abdominal pain, peripheral neuropathy, arthralgia/myalgia, cough, decreased appetite, dyspnea, infusion-related reactions, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, and extremity pain.
Serious adverse reactions occurred in 16% of patients who received margetuximab plus chemotherapy.
Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.1% of patients who received margetuximab plus chemotherapy, including viral pneumonia (0.8%) and aspiration pneumonia (0.4%).
In SOPHIA, left ventricular dysfunction occurred in 1.9% of patients treated with MARGENZA.
In Study 04, IRRs were reported by 13% of patients on the margetuximab plus chemotherapy arm.
